  "root_cause": "The loop condition 'i <= items.length' allows 'i' to reach a value equal to the array length, which is an index that does not exist.",
  "fixed_code": "const items = [\"pen\", \"book\", \"bag\"];\nfor (let i = 0; i < items.length; i++) {\n  console.log(items[i].toUpperCase());\n}",
  "explanation": "In JavaScript, array indices start at 0 and end at length minus 1. By using '<=' instead of '<', your code tried to access 'items[3]', which is undefined because the array only has indices 0, 1, and 2. Calling '.toUpperCase()' on an undefined value causes the crash.",
  "steps": [
    "Check the loop boundary condition to see if it exceeds the array index range.",
    "Add a console.log(i) inside the loop to see which index causes the error.",
    "Remember that the last valid index of an array is always length - 1."
  ],
  "tip": "Use a standard 'i < items.length' condition to safely stop before you go out of bounds.",
